work.title: The Life and Death of King Richard the Second

content.text: Enter John of Gaunt with the Duchess of Gloucester.

lines.plainText: Alas the part I had in Woodstock's blood

lines.text: Doth more solicit me than your exclaims
lines.plainText: Doth more solicit me than your exclaims

lines.text: To stir against the butchers of his life.
lines.plainText: To stir against the butchers of his life

lines.plainText: But since correction lieth in those hands

lines.text: Which made the fault that we cannot correct,
lines.plainText: Which made the fault that we cannot correct

lines.text: Put we our quarrel to the will of heaven,
lines.plainText: Put we our quarrel to the will of heaven

lines.text: Who, when they see the hours ripe on earth,
lines.plainText: Who when they see the hours ripe on earth

lines.text: Will rain hot vengeance on offenders' heads.
lines.plainText: Will rain hot vengeance on offenders' heads

lines.text: Finds brotherhood in thee no sharper spur?
lines.plainText: Finds brotherhood in thee no sharper spur

lines.text: Hath love in thy old blood no living fire?
lines.plainText: Hath love in thy old blood no living fire

lines.text: Edward's seven sons, whereof thyself art one,
lines.plainText: Edward's seven sons whereof thyself art one

lines.text: Were as seven vials of his sacred blood,
lines.plainText: Were as seven vials of his sacred blood

lines.text: Or seven fair branches springing from one root.
lines.plainText: Or seven fair branches springing from one root

lines.text: Some of those seven are dried by nature's course,
lines.plainText: Some of those seven are dried by nature's course

lines.text: Some of those branches by the Destinies cut;
lines.plainText: Some of those branches by the Destinies cut

lines.text: But Thomas, my dear lord, my life, my Gloucester,
lines.plainText: But Thomas my dear lord my life my Gloucester

lines.text: One vial full of Edward's sacred blood,
lines.plainText: One vial full of Edward's sacred blood

lines.text: One flourishing branch of his most royal root,
lines.plainText: One flourishing branch of his most royal root

lines.text: Is cracked, and all the precious liquor spilt,
lines.plainText: Is cracked and all the precious liquor spilt

lines.text: Is hacked down, and his summer leaves all faded,
lines.plainText: Is hacked down and his summer leaves all faded

lines.text: By envy's hand and murder's bloody axe.
lines.plainText: By envy's hand and murder's bloody axe

lines.text: Ah, Gaunt! his blood was thine! That bed, that womb,
lines.plainText: Ah Gaunt his blood was thine That bed that womb

lines.text: That metal, that self mould, that fashioned thee
lines.plainText: That metal that self mould that fashioned thee

lines.text: Made him a man; and though thou livest and breathest,
lines.plainText: Made him a man and though thou livest and breathest

lines.text: Yet art thou slain in him. Thou dost consent
lines.plainText: Yet art thou slain in him Thou dost consent

lines.text: In some large measure to thy father's death
lines.plainText: In some large measure to thy father's death

lines.text: In that thou seest thy wretched brother die,
lines.plainText: In that thou seest thy wretched brother die

lines.text: Who was the model of thy father's life.
lines.plainText: Who was the model of thy father's life

lines.text: Call it not patience, Gaunt; it is despair.
lines.plainText: Call it not patience Gaunt it is despair

lines.text: In suff'ring thus thy brother to be slaughtered,
lines.plainText: In suff'ring thus thy brother to be slaughtered

lines.text: Thou showest the naked pathway to thy life,
lines.plainText: Thou showest the naked pathway to thy life

lines.text: Teaching stern murder how to butcher thee.
lines.plainText: Teaching stern murder how to butcher thee

lines.text: That which in mean men we entitle patience
lines.plainText: That which in mean men we entitle patience

lines.text: Is pale cold cowardice in noble breasts.
lines.plainText: Is pale cold cowardice in noble breasts

lines.text: What shall I say? To safeguard thine own life,
lines.plainText: What shall I say To safeguard thine own life

lines.text: The best way is to venge my Gloucester's death.
lines.plainText: The best way is to venge my Gloucester's death

lines.text: God's is the quarrel; for God's substitute,
lines.plainText: God's is the quarrel for God's substitute

lines.text: His deputy anointed in His sight,
lines.plainText: His deputy anointed in His sight

lines.text: Hath caused his death, the which if wrongfully,
lines.plainText: Hath caused his death the which if wrongfully

lines.text: Let heaven revenge, for I may never lift
lines.plainText: Let heaven revenge for I may never lift

lines.text: An angry arm against His minister.
lines.plainText: An angry arm against His minister

lines.text: Where then, alas! may I complain myself?
lines.plainText: Where then alas may I complain myself

lines.text: To God, the widow's champion and defence.
lines.plainText: To God the widow's champion and defence

lines.text: Why then, I will. Farewell, old Gaunt.
lines.plainText: Why then I will Farewell old Gaunt

lines.text: Thou goest to Coventry, there to behold
lines.plainText: Thou goest to Coventry there to behold

lines.text: Our cousin Hereford and fell Mowbray fight.
lines.plainText: Our cousin Hereford and fell Mowbray fight

lines.text: O, sit my husband's wrongs on Hereford's spear,
lines.plainText: O sit my husband's wrongs on Hereford's spear

lines.text: That it may enter butcher Mowbray's breast!
lines.plainText: That it may enter butcher Mowbray's breast

lines.text: Or if misfortune miss the first career,
lines.plainText: Or if misfortune miss the first career

lines.text: Be Mowbray's sins so heavy in his bosom
lines.plainText: Be Mowbray's sins so heavy in his bosom

lines.text: That they may break his foaming courser's back
lines.plainText: That they may break his foaming courser's back

lines.text: And throw the rider headlong in the lists,
lines.plainText: And throw the rider headlong in the lists

lines.text: A caitiff recreant to my cousin Hereford!
lines.plainText: A caitiff recreant to my cousin Hereford

lines.text: Farewell, old Gaunt. Thy sometimes brother's wife
lines.plainText: Farewell old Gaunt Thy sometimes brother's wife

lines.text: With her companion, Grief, must end her life.
lines.plainText: With her companion Grief must end her life

lines.text: Sister, farewell; I must to Coventry.
lines.plainText: Sister farewell I must to Coventry

lines.text: As much good stay with thee as go with me!
lines.plainText: As much good stay with thee as go with me

lines.text: Yet one word more. Grief boundeth where it falls,
lines.plainText: Yet one word more Grief boundeth where it falls

lines.text: Not with the empty hollowness, but weight.
lines.plainText: Not with the empty hollowness but weight

lines.text: I take my leave before I have begun,
lines.plainText: I take my leave before I have begun

lines.text: For sorrow ends not when it seemeth done.
lines.plainText: For sorrow ends not when it seemeth done

lines.text: Commend me to thy brother, Edmund York.
lines.plainText: Commend me to thy brother Edmund York

lines.text: Lo, this is all. Nay, yet depart not so!
lines.plainText: Lo this is all Nay yet depart not so

lines.text: Though this be all, do not so quickly go;
lines.plainText: Though this be all do not so quickly go

lines.text: I shall remember more. Bid him—ah, what?—
lines.plainText: I shall remember more Bid himah what

lines.text: With all good speed at Plashy visit me.
lines.plainText: With all good speed at Plashy visit me

lines.text: Alack, and what shall good old York there see
lines.plainText: Alack and what shall good old York there see

lines.text: But empty lodgings and unfurnished walls,
lines.plainText: But empty lodgings and unfurnished walls

lines.text: Unpeopled offices, untrodden stones?
lines.plainText: Unpeopled offices untrodden stones

lines.text: And what hear there for welcome but my groans?
lines.plainText: And what hear there for welcome but my groans

lines.text: Therefore commend me; let him not come there
lines.plainText: Therefore commend me let him not come there

lines.text: To seek out sorrow that dwells everywhere.
lines.plainText: To seek out sorrow that dwells everywhere

lines.text: Desolate, desolate, will I hence and die!
lines.plainText: Desolate desolate will I hence and die

lines.text: The last leave of thee takes my weeping eye.
